such is the description given of the Lord known as Govinda."
Now, learn of the arrangement of Viṣṇu’s emblems:
in his left and right hands, and in front [of him], are the conch and the lotus.
Likewise, with his two rear hands, he holds a discus and two kaumodakī maces;
now hear the description of the one known as Madhusūdana.
He holds a lotus in his principal left hand and the Pāñcajanya conch in his right;
the mace is in the rear left hand, and the discus is in the rear right hand. (Pauṣkara 36.155)
Thus, indeed, there are three [forms] of the gods who are embodiments of knowledge;
but the second, due to its fourfold nature, possesses the brilliant luster of a ruby.
Now, the sequence of the three Pradyumna deities is stated;
listen indeed to the inclusion of their emblems along with the distinction of their colors. (Pauṣa 36.157)
In the front left hand there is a discus, and in another hand a mace;
in the back left hand a conch is remembered, and in the one following that, a lotus.
Understand that of the Lord known as Trivikrama,
Vāmana holds a mace in his left front hand, while the discus is in his primary right hand.
In the left hand, which is the western one, there is a lotus, and in that right hand, a conch;
for Śrīdhara, the mace is proclaimed to be in the principal left hand.
In the front right [hand] is the discus, and in the back left is the conch;
in the other two [hands], the supreme lotus and the discus with a radiance equal to ten million suns.
O twice-born one, these three forms, together with the Lord himself,
should be known as possessing the radiance of golden light, existing through the state of the fourfold self.
Therefore, understand also the triad of those whose forms are unceasing,
along with their bearing of emblems and their distinctions by color.
In the left front hand there is a lotus, and in the second [left hand] is the king of weapons;
then, in the two rear hands, right and left respectively, [he holds them].

One should understand that the lotus bud and the heavy mace reside in Padmanābha; the lotus called Cakra resides in the foremost [hand], while the other [lotus] is in the supreme hand on the crown of the head.
Dāmodara holds a mace in his left hand, a king of conchs in the one behind it,
and another auspicious mace in the frontmost left hand.
On the upper left [hand] is a conch shell; on the left [hand] is a discus;
and on the upper right [hand] is a lotus with the brilliance of the sun.
This group of forms is remembered as resembling the flax flower;
it too possesses a fourfold nature along with the deity Aniruddha.

Listen now to the establishment of the weapons—both those that are formless and those that possess form—for the sake of the sustenance of Viṣṇu, the Lord of All, within these three worlds. (Pauṣa 36.169)
O Great-minded One, the mace and the discus stand separately on either side, treading upon him with both hands and gazing at his face.
And Śaṅkhapāṇi and Śaṅkheśa form a pair with another weapon; that multitude of hands beginning from the second is endowed with various [implements].
It is endowed with a dust-whisk, a goad, a sword, a lotus, and other excellent weapons;
now hear of the sixteen forms of these various manifestations.
O best of the twice-born, one should contemplate the fivefold form of Pāñcajanya in the primary hand, and indeed the entire body as the mace and the discus. (Pauṣa 36.173)
With both hands pressed together, the face of the All-pervading Lord should be meditated upon by those devoted to Him as if drinking from an earthen vessel. Pausa 36.174.
Now, attend to this formless configuration of mantras;
it should be recollected through one's will, and even by the power of its graceful beauty.
Just as the state of the people of various lands has remained established since the beginning of creation,
so now the maintenance of both the formless and those possessing form is described together.
The pair [of hands] which were ordained for his two western arms have ascended from the region of the head and are gazing at the face of the Lord.
Holding a fan or similar object in his hand while awaiting an order, or with his hand tucked between his armpits, or else with the gesture of wonder; Paus. 36.178.
O Lotus-born One, it is joined with the mudrā known as *sampuṭa*;
indeed, the form of meditation consists of four faces and feet. Paushya 36.179.
O Brahmin, [the procedure] has been prescribed for all [beings], however, by virtue of necessity,
by the power of the practitioner's desire, and likewise indeed by the power of time.
Then those who were supplicants sat down upon couches of enjoyment;
situated upon seats of lotuses and water-wheels, they possessed the three abodes within their hearts.
Or else, with the previously mentioned twelve-syllable designations,
or with the six general mantras of the twice-born characterized by the six political expedients (ṣāḍguṇya).

Whoever worships with devotion, according to their own capacity or with their available wealth, being freed from all defects, attains that respective state which is free from suffering. (Pauṣa 36.183)
It is evident that in whichever field the [deity] has personally descended into the enclosure,
practitioners achieve success there by means of the specific name of that accomplishment.
O Lotus-born One, those who recite their own mantras, who are devoted, eternally pure, and intent on ritual action, [attain this] regarding the various forms of the gods. (Pauṣa 36.185)
Listen as I declare to you the convention beginning with the banner;
I shall speak of this triad of goddesses, which is proclaimed as beginning with Keśava.
It was adorned with a great Garuda-banner bearing a fluttering flag,
and with a large palm-tree emblem, as well as a plowshare and a lotus.
O twice-born one, that triad beginning with Govinda, which is indeed adorned by the banner known as the Makara and by Pradyumna, should be understood.
The triad beginning with Trivikrama is eternally adorned; it is marked by the deer-marked one (the Moon) and by Aniruddha.
And there is the triad ending with Dāmodara, beginning with Hṛṣīkeśa,
belonging to the omnipresent Lord Viśveśvara, who assumes forms according to his will.
All these have indeed been ordained together with their forms and sovereign powers by the gods who are lords of the three worlds, beginning with the Boar and the Man-Lion.
Then, O Lotus-born One, [the Lord appeared] with the fourfold forms beginning with Keśava, which are endowed with various manifestations, radiant with all virtues, and appropriate to each.

O Brahmin, [one should perform the rites] with those known as the swan, fish, horse, tortoise, lion, and boar, possessing the characteristics as described, according to one's capacity, and produced through ritual realization.
In this world, through their mode of life, they perform acts of worship and meditation for the sake of ascetics who are free from attachment, perfected beings, and residents of sacred fields.
Thus, with the aforementioned faces, human bodies, and great arms—
known as the Excellent Man, the Boar, and the Lion, and designated by the faces of the Horse— [the Lord appeared].
O one of stainless vision, [this] region of the earth was graced by the benevolent intent of Vāmananātha,
who assumed a dwarf form.
And the student who has completed his vows was adorned with the marks [of initiation], appearing in that very form which bestows the happiness of all pleasures. (Pauṣya 36.197)
By the Lord known by the name Trivikrama, whose form strides across the three worlds,
and known by the name Rāma, blazing with an axe in his hand.
O best of the twice-born, by these and other [deeds] which will be described, the removal of the burden from the earth has been performed many times.
Indeed, that entire collection of cosmic eggs, pervading both the interior and the exterior,
together with all the various manifestations and all the twice-born beings, [is encompassed by him].
Through the lords of the gods, both primary and secondary, who are called the sources and the dissolutions,
he— never abandoning his own nature— constantly assumes another form of his manifestation.
That reality which arises from a portion is indeed another manifestation;
endowed with various manifestations, it is the supreme collection of manifestations.
Listen to me as I speak correctly of those by whom the entire world is pervaded:
another Rāma, born of the kṣatriya caste, together with his three brothers. (Pauṣa 36.203)
He who, remembering "I am a man," was the slayer of the Rākṣasas, yet who, having accomplished his purpose, knew his own divine and supreme nature. (Pauṣa 36.204)
Furthermore, there was indeed Rāma, the wielder of the plow, who, together with the one whose self is Kṛṣṇa,
assumed the state of childhood and performed great divine deeds.
And know that the Lord Viṣṇu as Kalki, who descends to restore the lost Dharma, will appear in the Kali age upon the earth after slaying the hosts of Mlecchas. (Pauṣa 36.206)
The Lord Viṣṇu, whose nature is dharma, is eternal;
for he has indeed manifested as the first among men, ending with Kṛṣṇa.

He who always protects [the community] in this manner— endowed with his own duties, including the five times and the six acts, and joined with recitation and meditation— [attains the goal]. (Pauṣkara 36.208)
O Brahmin, after the manifestation of the All-pervading Lord, there appeared the fourfold-form Narayana Hari, the Blessed One known as Krishna. (Pausa 36.209)
It has been revealed by you in four ways; therefore, understand it as something else:
that Blessed One is the Universal Form, characterized by many bodies.
Among those, O Pauṣkara, one is indeed called Antarā, belonging to Kṛṣṇanātha;
and three others, which are primordial and imperishable, belong to him when he has descended into human form.
The glorious one has a thousand faces, a thousand feet, and a thousand hands;
he who bears both the manifest and the unmanifest, and gathers the immortals within his lineages.
And the great Lord of manifestation, whose navel is a lotus upon the waters,
effects both origin and dissolution through various yogas practiced in many different ways.
And know that the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha was another manifestation of that all-pervading Lord Padmanābha, occurring at the time of the Lord's manifestation.
The god who causes the Mandara mountain to fall, who likewise brought back the nectar of immortality,
who holds the jar of ambrosia, and whose body has the form of a woman.
Furthermore, O Mahāmati, the Blessed One himself cut off the head of that Rāhu into yet another form; thus was he divided into four parts.
Endowed with various manifestations, the most excellent among all manifestations,
the Lord of Lakṣmī is the supreme Master, a treasury of all auspiciousness.
The second [form] is the one with a serene self, who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men;
he is endowed with four forms of Lakṣmī and has Garuḍa as his seat.
Furthermore, endowed with glory, he occupies that seat or another one, free from any perceived distinctions;
he fulfills the mental dispositions of the gods and others, preceded by enjoyment.
He is the possessor of enjoyments, the slayer of Kālanemi, whose vehicle is the king of birds;
he has a thousand-spoked hand, is glorious, and is marked with the auspicious Śrīvatsa sign.
Is Kālavaiśvānara Śālinātha [the lord] of those dwelling in the waters?
[He is] the knower of the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti*) of the one who is...?
And indeed, of the embodied Lord.
He who indeed possesses a body of ego manifests through various distinctions;
he is the liberator of the lordly elephant from the crocodile of saṃsāra, which is characterized by its lack of essence.
The Lord Kapilākṣa, who is Adhokṣaja, is the instructor of knowledge;
and Brahmā, the embodiment of wisdom with four faces, is indeed honored by the world.
He who, indeed, is that constituent part characterized by all the marks and signs, and who always effects the dissolution at the end of the age; Paus_36.224.
Indeed, that manifestation of the Great Rudra named Śaṅkara occurred from the god Analaśāli,
who was situated at the very bottom of all things.
Lokeśvara is of peaceful form; they know him as the supreme Buddha, the one who has emerged from the qualities of intellect and who censures the fault of violence.
Know that the Sun and the Moon are the two embodied Lords who serve as the eyes of the Supreme Self, the God whose nature is known as Agni and Soma.
Taking that mouth as another deity, the supreme lord Agni,
purified by mantras, always receives the oblation preceded by clarified butter.
The presiding deity known as Vāyu eternally satisfies the entire universe of Brahmāṇḍa through the vital energy of Viśveśa.
And indeed, as the sustainer of the world through the nature of various aggregates,
these forms of the Blessed One abide within this triple world.
By means of various costumes and forms, characterized by various structures,
indeed by virtue of various functions and by virtue of various appearances.

Thus, by means of fabricated sounds and so forth, the Blessed One was propitiated in that very instant through a form resembling his own, for those who practice the recitation and meditation of that [mantra].
In its intended form, endowed with the six qualities,
having the nature of consciousness, eternal, and possessing a stainless essence as its own true nature.
O Mahāmati, she who exists everywhere for all those previously mentioned, out of a desire to bestow grace upon everyone, has filled the entire universe.
The eternal universal form of the manifestations beginning with Vāsudeva arises through the power of yogic sovereignty and by the will of Acyuta.
Knowing this, O Lotus-born One, you should not harbor astonishment in your heart,
for [the Lord] indeed manifests with various names through his clearly evident nature as the abyss.
When the form of the Blessed One is seen— whether manifested spontaneously or by other means—
and when he has descended into the midst of the earth by the path previously described.
In all the sacred fords (tīrtha), in various holy fields (kṣetra), on delightful mountain peaks, and in the caves situated among them; Pausa 36.238.
In forests rich with groves, in the regions of the netherworld,
in other worlds situated above, along with the gods and the most excellent of the Gandharvas.
Atheists who have transgressed the boundaries of conduct, who are possessed by the impurities of delusion and illusion,
are overcome by the defects of conceptual construction and rendered dull by their perverted intellects.
But those base individuals who touch the lotus-stalk of his feet sink for a long time into a terrible hell together with their ancestors. (Pausa 36.241)
Those whose minds are corrupted by worldly existence and who indeed seek the root of the gods of the six sense-bases shall suffer the severing of their heads.
The root, consisting of the power of fortitude, is difficult to perceive even for the gods;
how then could it be perceived by the deluded, since it has assumed the state of a material substance? (Pauṣa 36.243)
And how that supreme [deity] is independent through the measures and the objects of measurement,
by which this middle hexad is established by those born from the feet of the Lord of the Field (Kṣetreśa).

That state which consists of dwelling after having descended [into the world], while spontaneously conquering through divine qualities endowed with excellence and through powerful, natural qualities, by means of the Lords themselves.
Once grasped, it becomes perfectly stable and is even fashioned by those who have attained mastery;
yet, due to defects such as the divisions of the directions and so forth, it passes into other states.
Due to the greatness of his eternal presence, time proceeds in this world in an ever-increasing succession until the end of the kalpa.
O Mahāmati, she who grants the pacification of the wicked by her power and bestows accomplishment (siddhi) together with it, is the source of manly prowess and of those known as the Siddhas.
Therefore, even for the lords of reality who have descended of their own accord to the earth,
as well as for the devotees who fear saṃsāra, [they seek refuge] in the Lord of All.
Those who are to be visited and those who are to be honored should indeed be served at all times by those residing there who possess the qualities of the stages of life (āśrama).
When men who have attained their authority— through the knowledge of the rules for the end of initiation and so forth—
perform initiation for others, it becomes endowed with authority.
For the sake of propitiating Acyuta and for the attainment of the state of supreme bliss,
the worship of other deities was strictly forbidden at that very time.
For this is indeed the supreme commitment (samaya) for those whose nature is immeasurable jewels;
it is well-established as arising from the manifest form of the Supreme Lord.
Apart from the *vyūha* and that which is called the *vibhava*, there is no other form residing on earth to be worshipped by the wise, as has been stated previously. (Pauṣkara 36.254)
O best of the twice-born, in some places royal emblems are seen presided over by manifestations that are portions of the Blessed One, and they are likewise heard of.
O Great Sage, although it be so for Vaiṣṇavas, nevertheless they are not to be worshipped because of their opposition; for that [devotion] is not a Vaiṣṇava qualification.
Furthermore, those who have descended themselves as gods,
Siddhas, Skanda, Rudra, Mahendra, and others, are prohibited from being worshipped by them.
And the Inner Controller, the Supreme Person among all the gods, exists both in unmanifest form and in manifest form; for each [deity] has its own particular accomplishment. (Pauṣa 36.258)

O Brahmin, because of the power of devotion to the state of being and also from the attainment of one's own practice, having understood this intermingling of devotion, one should certainly not act in such a manner. (Pauṣkara 36.257)
One who desires the supreme goal should avoid with effort those brahmins known as Ekāyanas, who are devotees of Acyuta in truth.

Those who are single-mindedly devoted, established in the true reality, and do not worship other deities until the end of their bodies—those who worship Viṣṇu as their duty, without desire for fruit; (Pauṣkara 36.261)
And at the end of the body, O Lotus-born One, they attain the state of Vāsudeva;
others who perform sacrifices with mixed motives are known as mere semblances of devotees.
But those groups of various paths must be fully understood by you, O Brahmins, through worship;
therefore, one whose body has been perfected by the rite known as initiation— Pausa 36.263.
As long as he has the authority for recitation, he should be devoted to Nārāyaṇa;
intent upon the acts of recitation and fire-offerings, he remains seated, dedicated to hymns of praise.
At the end of the body, he shall indeed attain the world of Viṣṇu,
and having obtained an excellent birth once again, O best of the twice-born, he shall remain so from childhood.
One should be skilled in the actions of the Blessed One, devoted to them,
and absorbed in them, never aiming for a fruit even when faced with times of adversity.
"Having abandoned the body, one shall not undergo rebirth here again, O Pauṣkara.
Pauṣkara said:
"O Blessed One, Lord of the past and the future, [tell me] along with the sacred fields and the most excellent of fields."
And by those who, through their perfection, have pervaded the entire extent of the earth with the compendium of reality.
Beginning from the true reality known as Vāsudeva,
you should indeed explain it to me in due order, out of your constant desire to bestow grace upon all.

The Blessed One said: "O twice-born one, by means of my own self consisting of four aspects, established within the body known as the sixfold qualities (ṣāḍguṇya), my own station pervades everything up to heaven through the nature of the presiding deity."
She who is indeed the sovereign power of all, known as Īśvarī,
the leader of the people, [is endowed] with the primordial fourfold nature, distinguished by the divisions of knowledge and the rest.
And she is pervaded by the Great Self, whose form is light and whose mark is unmanifest;
she is the supreme divine Prakṛti, characterized by the single quality of sattva.
O Lotus-born One, Pūrṇā is present through the multitude of powers belonging to Vaibhavī,
together with another form and likewise as another manifestation.
Through seeds consisting of manifestations, within the aggregate of fourfold nature,
there exists the imperishable designation of the individual soul (*jīva*), the knower of the field (*kṣetrajña*), and the self (*ātman*).
Indeed, by the will of the Lord, that very [nature] always proceeds, having reached its support—
the eternal, unmanifest state known as the equilibrium of the three qualities.
Therein resides the Supreme Lord, known by the form of ego-consciousness (*abhimāna*),
who is clearly both manifest and unmanifest, the fourfold self, and the Lord of the world.
Two-armed, possessing a human form, resembling the sun in brilliance,
and adorned with banners, ornaments, and emblems such as the conch and the discus.
He abides in the unmanifest principle of the intellect (*buddhitattva*), yet is most manifest and all-pervading;
he has four forms, four faces, four arms, and four modes of being.
O Lotus-born One, having resorted to ego, he is joined with the manifest, imperishable marks extending to the banners. (Pauṣa 36.278)
All those beginning with Keśava are remembered as existing in various forms;
likewise, those beginning with Haṃsa, which I have described as consisting of six [aspects], are characterized by their respective accomplishments.

O Brahmin, having attained the principle of the mind (manas-tattva), these six, endowed with the qualities of perfect knowledge, again become otherwise, possessing the qualities of the sense organs (buddhīndriya).
Having assumed human bodies, these supreme lords remain established;
they are headed by Kalki, possess six arms, and include Vāmana and others who are lords of the twice-born.
But those qualities beginning with dharma and ending with the universal form (viśvarūpa), which are endowed with all attributes, always remain supported by the collection of the organs of action.
O Lotus-born One, they remain supported by the five subtle elements (tanmātra-pañcaka) which are to be consumed,
and by that collection of elements beginning with space (ākāśa).
O one of great intelligence, those foremost of the wise who were previously mentioned are indeed established by relying upon these remaining manifestations, along with the others yet to be described.
Just as [the sun], having undergone an eclipse, reaches a single region encompassing the three worlds,
so too does one attain the confluence of sacred fords on the land of the Kurus.
And with a supreme intent to favor them and with great compassion, O twice-born one,
he remembered at the time of death that the Buddhas were pervaded by the gods.

Those who possess the presiding deity, the earth as their limit, the body as the collection of principles, and are joined with the signified and the signifier—they too attain the supreme goal. (Pauṣa 36.287)
For it is by the power of the Blessed One, known as compassion, O twice-born one,
that he enters the affectionate kinsmen of a living being for the sake of establishing their connection.
O Mahāmati, by this rite he indeed brings about auspiciousness for one who is unconscious at a sacred ford, a sanctuary, or a field.
Pauṣkara said:
"O Lord, please now point out that place which has been occupied here for the sake of showing grace to all beings, together with the sacred fields and their presiding lords."
The Blessed One said:
"In the land of action (karmabhūmi), those fields which are auspicious for humans are likewise inaccessible even to them, except for the hosts of gods and siddhas. (Pauṣa 36.291)
Now, listen with constant and one-pointed attention to me regarding that region of the earth known as the Āryāvarta, which is designated as meritorious.
In a region bordering the Middle Country (Madhyadeśa), established on all four sides,
at the edge of the ocean’s waterline, within that vast expanse.
All the gods, beginning with Ādideva, who have descended since the beginning of creation along with their respective presiding deities, are characterized by manifest forms.
And in whatever region of the earth, from whatever source, each respective universal form has come and remained since the beginning of creation.
Indeed, they were accompanied by Kṣetrapa and likewise by Tīrtheśa;
for from that region of Devālaya, the lotus was blown [forth].
That which is pierced by the sound from "Bhava" is called the field (*kṣetra*);
it is the imperishable interval between the divine abodes and so forth. (Pauṣkara 36.297)
By this measurement, that which is equal to or slightly less than one krośa is to be known as Antarvedī for those whose souls are devoted to Nārāyaṇa. (Pauṣa 36.298)

In performing a sacrifice, in offering a *śrāddha*, in giving a gift, in departing [from this world], in worship, in recitation (*japa*), meditation, austerity, sacrifice, and even in the satiation of the sacrificial fire— *Pauṣa* 36.299.
O best of the twice-born, just as the light of a lamp situated in one place illuminates the region of the earth beyond it, so indeed does it act.
Having approached one's own field and the Lord of the Field,
embodied beings attain accomplishment both in this world and the next.
In that regard, first of all, attend now to the arrangement of the fourfold form and the assembly of other forms upon the earth.
Having taken recourse to the sacred field of Puṣkara, the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva remains eternally present there under the name Puṇḍarīkākṣa.

Thus, having arrived with all the excellent fields, the Lord of the Universe himself established the fourfold manifestation, beginning with the twice-born, at the sacrifice for the maintenance of creation.
Understand the differentiation of the four forms, numbering twelve, along with their sacred fields and associated pilgrimage sites. Pausa 36.305.
Keśava, the destroyer of afflictions, dwells on earth in two forms:
in his manifest form he is Govinda, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
He remained stationed on a portion of the ground in the vicinity of the mountain.
O Brahmin, O destroyer of the world's sins, even in the place called Vṛndāvana, Viṣṇu is established in two ways: as Kamalodbhava and by the name Viṣṇupada.
Having reached the mountain named Mandara, Madhusūdana descended and remained there out of compassion for all living beings.
O Lotus-born one, the God of gods, Trivikrama, having taken recourse to the waters of the Yamunā, remains there bestowing a happy destiny upon men.
O Lotus-born One, another form known as Vāmana has descended from your own essence and rests upon Mount Sahya for the sake of pacifying the sorrow of living beings.
Having reached the waters called Narmadā, which destroy all sin,
the god Śrīdhara is established there, as is Kauṇḍale, together with Śrī.
But the Blessed Lord Hṛṣīkeśa, though established upon the earth by his own nature, O Lotus-born One, resides in the field known as Dhvajā at Kubjāmraka on the mountain Dharādhara.
Padmanābha, the Lord of Mādhya, having descended, remained stationed there,
taking recourse in the southern direction near the shore of the ocean.
O Brahmin, the Blessed Lord Dāmodara has come from his own essential nature and dwells on Mount Revataka for the sake of the welfare of those whose minds are purified.
O best of the twice-born, having reached the temple of the universe together with these various forms and manifestations, [one perceives] the established state of others as well. (Pauṣa 36.326)
O Greatly Intelligent One, understand this with an attentive mind:
know that the King of Swans is worshipped by the Siddhas and immortals in Śvetadvīpa. (Pauṣa 36.327)
The Blessed One is of the nature of a fish in the waters, of the nature of a horse in the submarine fire (Vaḍavāmukha),
of the nature of a tortoise in the netherworld (Rasātala), and of the nature of a lotus in the Vindhya forest.
The self of the Lord of Beasts, the destroyer of the sins of all embodied beings, is to be known there in that very field in the form of a boar. (Pauṣa 36.319)
On the auspicious bank of the Ganges, frequented by gods and siddhas,
the Lord whose eyes are like the finest gold resides within the great golden mountain.
The Lord Mīnavaktra (the Fish-faced) resides at Naubandhana-giri;
the god Aśvaśiras at Kṛṣṇāśva; and [the god] Kṣamārcita at Kṣitikṣetra.
On the coastal region bordering the salt ocean, frequented by the Siddhas,
the Blessed One resides with the face of a tortoise, bearing the conch and the discus.
O twice-born one, when the purification was completed, Nṛhari likewise remained in three ways in the city of Ujjayinī, at the place known as Viśākhamūla.
At Kokāmukha there is Varāha; at Vārāha, the best of mountains; at Kandamālā, Viveśa; at Kulakukṣi and Himācala. (Pausa 36.324)
He who exists as Vāmana and Kharvamūrti through his universal form (vaiśvarūpya),
in the Middle Country along the Gaṅgā and in Kurukṣetra at Pauṣkara.
Having reached the Yamunā lineage, there exists a great other manifestation known as Trivikrama, whose body traversed the three worlds.
O twice-born one, on that best of mountains called Mahendra,
the Blessed One known as Rāma stands with axe in hand, the ender of the kṣatriyas.
On Mount Citrakūṭa, the great Rāma, the destroyer of the Rākṣasas,
whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals, remains established there.
Rāma, who is indeed another Sīrapāṇi, remains in the auspicious human regions, causing the waters of the Yamunā to whirl.
Furthermore, on that island in the ocean known as Dvārakā, which is worshipped by the immortals,
dwells the Blessed One Kṛṣṇa, the soul of all, the Supreme Lord.
The Lord Kalki Viṣṇu, being praised by the twice-born,
remained there with a restrained mind after reaching the river Vipāśā.
The high-souled one, whose very form is Dharma, dwells in Dharmāraṇya, which is honored by the gods;
devoted to bestowing grace, he remains there, worshipped by the worlds.
Known as Narasaṃjña, the Lord of the World remains eternally present in those delightful regions that are worshipped by the Siddhas.
On the mountain named Govardhana, Lord Hari, the sovereign of all, resides;
he is worshipped at that sacred site during the seasonal migrations of the cattle.
And in Śāligrāma, O twice-born one, the Blessed One likewise resides by means of a portion of his earthly nature in the forest named Rājendra,
under the designation Devavrata.
O Brahmin, another Kṛṣṇa, possessing four forms, descended to the surface of the earth and remained at Piṇḍāraka, liberating people from their evil deeds.
O Lotus-born One, the Lord in his universal form resides in Śvetadvīpa, Kurukṣetra, on the Himavat mountain, and also among men at the sacrificial altar.
In the ocean of milk, Padmanābha is situated upon the serpent Śeṣa as his couch; from the lotus born from his navel, the Grandfather (Brahmā) himself has arisen.
Relying upon form in four ways, she alone exists throughout this entire universe; understand correctly how she acts for the welfare of all the worlds. (Pauṣa 36.339)
O Brahmin, having reached his bed situated in the depths of Pātāla,
he assumes a fiery form and at the end withdraws the entire world.
Having resorted to the foot of the banyan tree at Prayāga, which is honored by the gods,
and having reached that divine tree, he made the entire world into a single ocean.
O twice-born one, that Blessed One remains there on the bank of the earth;
one should meditate upon Him reclining beneath the banyan tree, who bestows the divine state.
On a lofty portion of the Himalayas known as Bhṛgu,
he who is the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha remained upon the surface of the earth.
In the field of earth consisting of milk and water, frequented by gods and asuras,
the Lord dwells upon the peak of Mount Mandara, honored by the gods.
In that very place resides the god Amṛtajit, served by the Siddhas;
he assumes a beautiful form and likewise holds a vessel of nectar.
The Conqueror of Death stands among the perfected ones, the sages, and the gods;
he is the one who can divide into two the Lord who is accompanied by his hosts and whose vehicle is Garuḍa.
The Lord resides at Sāligrāma on the branch of a *sāla* tree,
upon the ridge of Mount Trikūṭa, which is accessible to those who travel through the sky.
Under the very pretext of lifting the elephant, the Lord who is the Sovereign of Śvetadvīpa remained there, having descended and established himself under the name Aprameya.
At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, on a delightful spot of earth,
the Lord, the eater of sacrifice, dwells at Naimiṣa, which is honored by the Siddhas.
The Lord Ananta resides, having taken refuge in the Saindhava forest;
while the Lord of Gods, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, dwells in the region known as Daṇḍaka-araṇya.
And he, the infallible one known as Śauri, remained in the region of Utpalāvartaka, intent on the victory of those who desired to conquer the host of Rākṣasas.
At the confluence of the Kṣitī, Samudra, and Sindhu rivers, a place frequented by the Siddhas,
the Blessed One resides as a teacher of knowledge for the sake of pacifying suffering.
Having reached the field of Sūkara, the Lord whose vehicle is Garuḍa stood mounted upon Garuḍa, marked by the *pārijātaka* tree held in his hand.
O Pauṣkara, together with the Siddhas and the hosts of gods, he who is named the Lord of the Gods of Gods [resided] even in the sky upon the summit of Mount Hasti.
O Mahāmati, having reached a certain region, the granter of boons, Vaikuṇṭha, stands in Magadhā with a garland and water in his hands.
The Blessed One, the Supreme Person, whose nature is inconceivable, was stationed on Mount Gandhamādana in the sacred region of Oḍḍīya.
The Lord, established in the vow of Śipiviṣṭa under the name Śipiviṣṭa,
[resided] on that auspiciously marked portion of land extending as far as the ocean.
Having assumed the form of Kapila, the Lord Vāsudeva remained there;
and having descended from his own essential nature, he became the Prajāpati known as Brahmā.
O Brahmin, having reached Maṇibandha, he remains eternally present in the region of Magadha, residing upon the earth of Great Enlightenment.
The Lord of the World, the God of gods, Janārdana, is established as the self;
he is the twice-born one who is the embodiment of the pride residing in the right eye of the god.
The Lord known as Sūrya is situated upon the Golden Mountain; the omnipresent Acyuta, whose body is composed of self-conceit, resides in the left eye.
The Blessed One, known as Soma, while at the hermitage of Somatīrtha,
remained in the form of Agni within the submarine fire (vaḍabānala), O Invincible One.
O Brahmin, the Lord who brings an end to the asuras shines in the sky as the soul of all things;
moreover, that god is named Viṣṇu, adorned with many weapons.
Indeed, Jayā resides in Ujjayinī for the conquest of the sins of men,
while [another] is situated in the auspicious region of Kāśmīra, in the sacred field known as Cakradhara.
But the Blessed One Cakrapāṇi stands there, the bestower of liberation upon his devotees;
and at Pauṣkara, he is known as Surottama, bearing a mace in his hand.
Know that he is always present at Gaṅgādvāra together with the gods—
he who has four arms, four forms, four faces, and four states of existence.
The eternal Lord Viṣvaksena resides at Piṇḍāraka,
as well as in the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, having reached that auspicious region of the earth.
And having come from his own domain, he approached the god named Viśveśvara,
who was stationed in the field called Sātatrana, which was filled with perfected beings and Vidyādharas.
The Lord of the World, known as Svāmī, resides on the bank of the Mandākinī;
in the great yoga of the Bhallātaka tree, he bestows liberation upon those who meditate.
O Brahmin, in the subterranean realm (rasātala) known as Nṛsiṃha, situated on the bank of the Devikā,
the Lord Sarveśvara resides under the name Ripukṣaya.
In the region of the earth known as Śaṅkara, which is frequented by all the gods,
the Lord of the World, the embodiment of knowledge, dwells, bestowing auspiciousness upon men.
On earth, in the field of the ancestors, the Blessed One, the Soul of the Universe, dwells under the name Janārdana, O Brahmin, liberating beings from the three debts.
"O Lotus-born One, these incarnations have been described to you in brief;
by them, the surface of the earth has been pervaded again and again by you yourself."
O Lotus-born One, with a mind intent on favoring worldly beings,
one should constantly perform the recitation of those [names] that are otherwise inaccessible at the three junctions of the day.
One should form the intention (or indeed should act) toward visiting and even looking upon those Mlecchas in those lands, as well as the fields and other sites upon the earth there. (Pausa 36.375)
Indeed, they should always be viewed by the seers, gods, and perfected ones as being free from confusion within their own great hermitages.
In sacred reservoirs of water and in various places upon the earth,
all things possess the form of the Blessed One, characterized by the manifestations of his sovereign power.
Those who were liberated and those others who had departed, having themselves reflected with their own intellects,
remained established according to the rules, accompanied by mantras and possessing true valor.
By means of their persistence, those things which are of various kinds— designated as past, future, and so forth—
are indeed [distinguished] by way of their configuration, known as gentle, fiery, or both.
Indeed, together with the various manifestations of his weapons and emblems—consisting of the splendor of his divine play and bestowing happiness upon the mind—[he appeared]. Pausa 36.380.
And the region of the earth was likewise adorned by devoted men who had been graced [by him], as well as by the Siddhas and others, just as it has been described.
These, beginning with Ādideva, are declared to be the lords of the principles (tattveśas);
they are established within the supreme principle of the Blessed Lord through the differentiation of the principles.
Just as the rays of the sun, just as the mass of flames from a fire,
and just as the waves of the ocean, even so it is with you, O Lotus-born One.
The universal consciousnesses are eternally pure, all-pervasive, and supreme lords;
resting upon the existence of reality, they are fully adorned with knowledge and other [perfections].
Endowed with the eightfold powers beginning with *aṇimā*, they indeed abide by their own nature and constantly maintain their presence throughout all the paths and stages.
For the liberation of all beings, and especially on this earth,
[this is taught] starting from the time of the universal origin until the end of the dissolution.
In sacred fields and on the banks of holy fords, by means of the *śabdabrahman*—whether through a general mantra or through the self that manifests as its transformation—Paus. 36.387.
Then, for the benefit of all the worlds, he assumed a form that was both manifest and otherwise, composed of the earth-element, descended yet imperishable.
In this world known as Āyatana, yogins attain perfection;
for, after a period of time, the submergence of individual manifestations occurs.

And there, the lords of yoga, the gods, and the perfected ones (siddhas) constantly maintain their presence through the state of power, having recollected that form which consists of that very essence.
And those who possess the power of mantras establish there a manifest form arising from the extraction of the mountain's essence, performing the penetration into it.
That which is indeed remembered as the interval between the two names beginning with "Acyuta" is the very form of Him who is present and who bears a body of sound. (Pauṣkara 36.392)
When mantras—whether they are of diverse natures, manifest in their own forms or unmanifest, restrained, or functioning according to one's will—are [employed],... Pausa 36.393.
The forms and configurations of the Supreme Lord are otherwise;
indeed, in this world, that which is eternal is known both as the manifest and the unmanifest.
In this way, O Pauṣkara, the eternality of the sense-bases (āyatana), as well as their beginninglessness, incalculability, and vastness, have been fully revealed.
O twice-born one, those who have arisen as my manifestation are indeed established by virtue of their individuality;
yet even without that individual form, I exist through the imperishable nature of the Word.
For other excellent sages, O Brahmin, having seen that delightful place, perceived it as being composed of both the nature of sound and the nature of the manifestation of sound elsewhere.
Having established a firm stability there through both action and mind, one should dwell by pure, stainless water abounding with trees and medicinal herbs.
Having inspected a stone of auspicious marks, or one brought from elsewhere, and having commissioned a craftsman born of the lineage of Viśvakarman; Paus_36.399.
Having fashioned a beautiful lotus-footprint seal upon this earth, which is the womb of Viṣṇu, the Lord of All; Paus_36.400.
Likewise, O Mahāmati, there are other sages in their respective abodes who bear the marks of Hari, preceded by the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus.
Having established their residence there through actions purified by devotion, other best of the twice-born, whose minds were nourished by devotion, [remained]. (Pauṣa 36.402)
And out of a desire for the welfare of their devotees,
they establish their dwellings in the previously mentioned regions and in those fashioned by the Siddhas and others.
And among the thousands of mudrās beginning with the Sahasrāra-mudrā that have been sealed, and during the worship of the Great Buddha with stones cast from the beginning of creation; Pausa 36.404.
Having performed the appropriate ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in the form of consecration (*saṃskāra*),
they perform the daily worship according to the prescribed rules at the three times of day.

With excellent mantras preceded by the Ṛg and Sāma Vedas, consisting of twelve syllables, for the sake of attaining the state of the Blessed One and for the disciples and others to obtain auspiciousness. (Pauṣa 36.406)
In this way, O Puṣkarasambhūta, all the villages and provinces,
the cities and towns of kings, and those auspicious places renowned upon the earth [were established].
By the sages, by pure men, and by the Lord himself, they were brought to the nature of meritorious states for the sake of compassion toward his devotees. (Pauṣa 36.408)

O twice-born one, she remains through her various manifestations and arrays, desiring to bestow grace; yet when harm from thieves and the like occurs, she is present within [the victim]. (Pauṣa 36.409)
The mantras, such as the previous mantras and others, which were previously restrained there,
remain having abandoned the physical form within the space of the aperture of Brahmā.
As long as no remedial rite has been performed, that which was previously declared to be stationary increases;
otherwise, the great defect grows for half a day or a full day.
For all practitioners born in that region, as well as for the king,
[the rite should be performed] by the best of the twice-born and others, or by merchants, or even by householders.
The guides and the lord of men performed the *bhayanārāna* rite,
which consists of a collection of mantras intended for the pacification of the sins of all.
Indeed, for the welfare of all, one who would constantly perform the worship of individual images in secluded shrines for the sake of Dharma— Paus 36.414.
For those beings who have attained fullness, there shall be the pacification of faults, the destruction of all suffering, and the destruction of great delusion.
For that which is indeed the infallible form, characterized by its sovereignty over Brahmā,
is endowed with specific qualities and possessed of portions of divine glory.
Prajāpati, having approached him as he was reflected upon the mirror of his intellect,
brought him within the range of his own son’s hearing.
And for one who has been perfected through oblations and other rites, and consecrated by the preceptors,
the secondary form of the Lord indeed manifests there before long.
But at the time of its formal arrangement by the great-souled reciter,
such is the beginninglessness [established] regarding substances, qualities, and forms.

Indeed, one whose vision has attained perfection regarding the elements simultaneously on the ground does not fall into forgetfulness regarding the universe, as it rests upon the intellect of an artisan.
For he assumes a form endowed with auspicious marks for his devotees,
according to the specific desire of each, indeed, by the power of their internal devotion.
O wise one, know that the great, imperishable image which the self-manifested has revealed on earth—known as Brahmā, Rudra, and the Sole Sun—is indeed that very [reality]. (Pauṣa 36.422)
"O lotus-eyed one, that which was described as abiding in the various manifestations and endowed with diverse forms— indeed, it is to be propitiated in that very same way through the intellect."
Whether seated or standing during worship or meditative concentration,
others remain fixed in various postures, established within forms that dispel darkness.
And by his own will, he bears two marvelous marks:
with each of his two hands, he holds four [objects] hanging down from them.
By means of gathering the primary weapons—the conch, discus, mace, and lotus—in the very order previously specified for Lokeśa and the others, [one should proceed]. Paus 36.426.

The *jyā* and other [mudrās] may be performed at will, while others are indicated by arms extended horizontally; through the raising of the arms (*udbhujatva*), they signify the spiritual attainment of those who are exceedingly devoted.
But for those whose burden of devotion is slight,
that divine state of the Great Self— which indeed resides within as the ultimate attainment— is situated in a transverse position.
For those men who have lost their devotion while seeking refuge with the Vyābhis,
the attainment of heaven comes from Bhujavṛnda and others through their mouths.
O Brahmin, although I am always equal toward all beings, I shall indeed teach through reasoning that my devotees attain perfection. (Pauṣa 36.430)
Or those images which have been duly consecrated by other excellent kings, according to the rules, using the eight distinct classes of letters beginning with *brāhmaṇa*.

The manifestation consisting of a reflection, whether by oneself or by Acyuta, as well as movement without the removal of defects and without peace—[these constitute the nature of the soul]. (Pauṣkara 36.432)
A wound caused by portents and other such defects brings about the destruction of the king; however, once the re-establishment of those whose mantras have set has been performed, [the danger ceases].
O Pauṣkara, although their arising occurs constantly for the sake of peace,
they are meditated upon by the lords of teachers as resembling the sun, the moon, and fire.
And the lords of mantras, perfected through the resonance of the *praṇava*, enter [the body] and,
after a short period of time, draw forth their own supernatural power (*vibhūti*).
Indeed, having had their defects destroyed, they were rendered free from obstacles and pure once more;
they were then established by the most perfected ones in sacred fords, holy fields, and forests.

Those who, out of delusion, seek to prevent the configuration, the measurement, and the form of the manifestation of the multitude of manifestations—which exists as a defect persisting over time—[commit a grave error]. (Paus 36.437)
And at the time of their end, they sink into a terrible and unbearable darkness;
therefore, this [practice] is for those with meager wealth and those possessed of little wisdom. (Pauṣa 36.438)
Those who desire their own welfare must avoid the god without him,
for the Lord of the World himself has descended and remains just as he was.
Thus, when it has been grasped and remains firm, even if it is conceptualized by those who have not attained realization,
it does not undergo alteration through defects such as doubt, partiality, and the like.
Due to the greatness of his eternal presence, time proceeds in this world in an ever-increasing succession until the end of the kalpa.
She who, through her immeasurable prosperity, splendor, fame, and activity,
grants the pacification of the wicked, and indeed bestows perfection along with her power.
And there, O Mahāmati, are the bases of human power known as Siddhas,
who have themselves descended here upon this earth as lords of reality.
Thus, O Lotus-born One, I have revealed to you the secret concerning the lords of the fields together with the fields themselves, for the sake of the liberation of living beings. (Pauṣa 36.444)
And for those living beings seeking fruits who serve the Lord of the Field in every field,
they attain their desired goal right here, which is imperishable.
Now, listen to the secret concerning those great lords of the fields who are born upon the surface of the earth in the [age] called Pralaya. Paus_36.446.

By means of the seeds of the principles—beginning with knowledge and the rest, including the powers such as atomization (aṇimā), both the unmanifest and those ending with earth, which are to be adopted and endowed with the reality of Brahman—[one attains the goal]. // Paus 36.447 //
Or, having descended into the world, they indeed manifest themselves before creation;
thus, out of a desire to bestow grace upon all, they appear spontaneously in the form of objects.
At the time of the withdrawal of the circle of the earth, together with the sustainers of the field,
they abide within the principle of Īśvara by His will.
And at the time of the manifestation of the universe, they speak of a prior manifestation,
along with birth from the genus, as well as suffering arising from the body and its location.
How can one be liberated from such defects as mental sufferings preceded by mental and physical ailments, which are likewise unbearable? [Without you, how? Paus 36.451.
Whether through the favor of the field-born [deity] or through the favor of those with intense devotion and so forth, devotion becomes manifest for one who understands right knowledge. Pausa 36.452.
And at the end, O twice-born ones, the realization arises within the field of Acyuta;
yet those who are non-devotees, the foremost of atheists, do not desire it amidst their conceptual constructions. (Pauṣa 36.453)
Discrimination regarding the Puruṣa and other principles arises from the fruit of the Lord; indeed,
one who has been awakened should not abandon the purpose of the Puruṣa.
And life in this world is joined with the activities of Brahmins;
yet the Lord is capable of removing that [bondage] through various kinds of sacrifices.
The existence of that [reality], accompanied by its direct realization, is attained by those best of men who are faithful and devoted, having received it from the mouth of the Guru.
One should know the Self by means of the self; therefore, [know] the omniscient Lord, as well as that beginningless conceit which is material and born of the quality of sattva.
The terrible characteristic of *asmitā* (egoism), which always bestows what is desired, should be understood by the self through the self for as long as it has not been fully realized. (Paus 36.458)
For just as seeds that have been sown at the proper time yield abundant fruit,
so it is with those who have practiced [virtue].
And not in fields or sacred precincts.
"Furthermore, through the power of practice over many births, the exhaustion of karma will surely occur.
Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, titled "The Investigation of the Abodes," in the Pauṣkara-saṃhitā, a Great Upaniṣad within the glorious Pāñcarātra.
(Total number of verses: 461) Now begins the thirty-seventh chapter.
Pauṣkara said:
And, O Lord of the World, [he performed] the placement of stones marked with footprints, as well as those marked with wheels and lotuses, preceded by the ritual consecration. (Pauṣa 37.1)
O Lord of the World, I now desire to know about these supports and others as well, and likewise about the stones that have been established since beginningless time. (Pauṣa 37.2)
And by householders or forest-dwellers who have obtained the marks of the Supreme Lord, such as the conch and other insignia, for the purpose of worship; Paus 37.3.
Furthermore, for the accomplishment of sacrifices such as these,
please instruct me on the preparation of both movable and immovable materials.
The Blessed One said:
"In the past, the material was prepared by a self-restrained artisan,
having been purified through consecration with substances previously empowered by mantras."
O Lotus-born One, wherever a particular [deity] is appropriate, one should perform its placement there; thus, until the end of the power of grace, the manifestation occurs through perception.
The presence of the mantras should be effected upon a mobile seat alone; however, the temporary restraint and the worship therein are prescribed for that occasion. (Pauṣkara 37.7)

O Pauṣkara, beginning from the foundational power (ādhāra-śakti), the complete restraint of the entire collection of mantras is always prescribed for all [practitioners] once they have become well-stabilized.
Having invoked [the deity] there, one should worship the mantra, and after having worshipped, one should dismiss it again;
for it is not beneficial to worship the mantra outside of the time of worship, O Lotus-born One.
Because it is accomplished through a proper cause,
the Supreme Lord is here restrained by knowledge at the time of bringing flowers and other offerings every day.
But he who is intent on bestowing grace remains right there, like the sound of the ether (kha),
having attained a state of identity with the moving image.

The arrangement of mantras on the pedestal is prescribed as being like that of a movable pedestal; or, for one that is very stable or of a single origin, it is performed even in the absence [of a movable one]. Paus. 37.12.
O Pauṣkara, the placement (nyāsa) of the mantras prescribed for the stable pedestal is indeed performed from the feet up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) for the mobile image. Paus_37.13.
One should indeed perform the arrangement of the primary principles (tattvas), beginning with earth and ending with the feet, or from the Unmanifest (avyakta) down to the earth. (Pauṣkara 37.14)
One should apply the mantra consisting of all the principles (tattvas), or simply that which is predominant within its heart, as an inseparable cause of the principles.

Now, when the occasion for worship has arrived, one should employ the system of mantras and tantras for the sake of removing insentience and [awakening] the multitude of mantras pertaining to reality.

O Brahmin, having invoked that mantra—which is the very life-force, eternal, pure, ever-risen, complete with its limbs, and adorned with the sectarian marks and other signs—[one should proceed]. (Pauṣkara 37.17)
Having withdrawn [the deities] residing there, or when the worship has been completed,
one should perform the withdrawal of the mantra-arrangement that was previously described.
The expulsion of those who occupy sacred sites and holy fields is ordained, whether the consecrated image be permanently installed in a temple or even in one's own home. (Pauṣa 37.19)
Otherwise, one should perform its suppression upon the tongue and other such parts,
together with the mantras of the supporting seats and one's own identifying marks.
One should perform this specific rite for unstable foundations;
however, when that which has been described has been successfully accomplished and the Supreme Lord has been installed.
Then one should perform the secondary piercing (anuvedha) from the base up to the crest (śikhā),
by means of the thread of the power of capability and by the imperishable Lord.
When it exists, the multitude of mantras does not abandon that which has been restored by means of [the rites of] the reflection and so forth, even after the lapse of time. (Pauṣkara 37.23)
Whether unawakened or awakened, whatever man installs an image—whether it be another [image] or one made of material substance—in that sacred abode; ||| Paus_37.24 |||
And immediately thereafter, that [consciousness] arises permeated by that cognition;
for such is the nature of knowledge in these three worlds, O Lotus-born One. (Pauṣkara 37.25)
As long as the moon and stars exist,
this world-system remains as a collection of sense-bases, wherein the abode of the realm of beings is established and frequented by the perfected ones.
Therefore, one who knows that, who knows reality, who is devoted, faithful, and always a believer, should not lead those unaccomplished ones toward a state of impurity.
Having recognized that the single reversal of fortune arising from the passage of time is something that can be effectively remedied through efforts, he acted out of fear of its disappearance.
Having received that command preceded by the vows from Prasanna and the others,
one should perform the worship beginning with the Great Yoga (Mahāyāga) and ending with the *pūrṇāhuti*, using the syllable *praṇava*.
Having performed the ritual gift and having seated another upon the seat, the Supreme Lord arises in that very body in a different form. (Pauṣkara 37.30)
Disease, thieves, famine, and the destruction of the kingdom and cities— these,
as well as the present and future calamities of the country caused by floods and other disasters.
If the movement is performed according to the prescribed rule, it shall not bring about anything undesirable;
one may then perform the re-union either elsewhere or in that very same place.
According to the procedure prescribed in the scriptures, one should properly awaken the mantra with a preceding festival; however, one should awaken the tantra together with its ritual action.
When [the mind] is established in the two equal and peaceful states within an inexhaustible basis,
whatever fault arises for the mover due to shifting away from the prescribed method belongs to that mover.
However, for that [image] intended for oblations, worship, and giving, one should bring it to a state of equilibrium before its installation;
having made the image very stable and immovable, one should then set it down there.
One should perform the gift of cows, land, and gold according to one's ability; [the image] may be made of metal, clay, stone, or wood, and should not be transferred onto cloth or similar materials.

If the image of the Blessed One suddenly assumes a state of witheredness, it is due to the reversal of proper procedures, the omission of its rites, or worship performed at an improper time. (Pauṣa 37.37)
There will be great danger for the kingdom, as well as for the worshiper and the people;
therefore, [one should practice] that supreme mantra which is complete with its ancillaries and purified according to the tantra.
One should offer libations for seven days in succession into the water-pot, the mandala, and the fire;
during the seasons of Hemanta and Śaiśira, one should worship the divine image made of stone.
Having bathed and worshipped her according to the prescribed ritual,
and having wrapped her in fine garments, one should then [anoint her] with the sacrificial offering of cow-products (gavya-havis).
Having brought it to a state of solid mass from the base upward, one should color it with sandalwood and the like,
and adorn it with flowers made of leaf-cutting (*patraccheda*) or even those fashioned from cotton (*picu*).
And with other auspicious materials originating from various regions— white, yellow, and so forth,
dried by shade and air, green, and combined with various types [of fragrant substances].
Having performed the worship as prescribed, together with various ornaments, and having wrapped [the image] in a thick, white cotton cloth; Paus 37.43.
With saffron, or with a pure woolen blanket, or with white,
very thick, unwashed, and new [cloth].
When the cold season has indeed passed, one should remove the woolen blanket for the sake of purifying the foremost of the twice-born and those kings of purified soul. (Pauṣa 37.45)
He should grant the requests of his devotees, such as the citizens and others, in due order;
for their prosperity, for the pacification of inauspiciousness, and for their protection, he should grant their prayers in sequence.
For the victory over untimely deaths and for the pacification of diseases,
during the onset of the summer season, one should [bathe] every day with cool water.
One should perform the bath according to the prescribed procedure in due order,
using a powder made of lentils, black gram, turmeric, and śāli rice.
Having massaged him thoroughly, washed him, and anointed him with sacrificial oblation and other unguents, he should make him clean with a cloth and white sandalwood paste. (Pauṣa 37.49)
Then that dwelling should be washed with cold water;
having swept it, one should apply an external coating of cow dung.
Having scattered leaves, flowers, white water-lilies, blue lotuses, and red lotuses,
one should fan the image of the Infallible One with palm-leaf fans moistened with water.
Having praised him with various hymns in a loud voice,
O Lotus-born One, he then circumambulated him twice or four times.
It is neither one, nor five, nor three in number, nor is it anything irregular in its calculation;
for the Blessed Lord Hari is indeed equal toward all.
The renunciant (saṃnyāsī) should perform prostrations like a staff toward all directions, accompanied by circumambulation, rising up many times before him. (Pauṣa 37.54)

For those such as the *snātaka* and others, this very same practice is prescribed; indeed, it should be performed with a mind endowed with devotion together with the internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*). (Pauṣa 37.55)

A householder should daily perform prostrations accompanied by circumambulation, touching the ground with his forehead, back, head, knees, the surface of his forehead, his chest, and his hands. (Pauṣa 37.56)
Mentally recollecting the eight-syllable mantra repeatedly upon the expansive ground, he stood before the Blessed One on a patch of earth that had become a narrow space.
But as one should perform [this] with devotion, having joined the palms in *añjali*, one should meditate upon the Lord of All while trembling at the region of the heart and the head. (Pauṣa 37.58)
By performing this rite according to the prescribed method, or even according to one's own ability,
a person devoted to the practice of devotion attains the fruit as desired.
Free from desire, those who behold the Lord of the World with devotion, honored by his devotees, shall attain the eternal abode worshipped by the gods. (Pausa 37.60)
And those who rejoice with faith shall also partake in that fruit; for them,
the inexhaustible destruction of saṃsāra comes about through the exhaustion of karma.
For it is by means of these two methods, and not otherwise by any other way, that [the goal is attained]:
from the complete ritual section (kriyākāṇḍa) together with the mantras, which possesses five characteristics.

Through the thorough knowledge of perfect awakening and through being colored by devotion to the Blessed One, he who is eternally absorbed in the Blessed One in deed, mind, and speech— (Pauṣkara 37.63)
But one who possesses authority within the teaching shall abide in reality,
knowing the supremacy of this scripture which bestows liberation and is imperishable.
"Thus, he soon attains purification from previously accumulated evil deeds.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Examination of the Sanctuary," in the *Pauṣkarasaṃhitā*, a great Upaniṣad within the illustrious *Pāñcarātra*.
(Total number of verses: 64) Now begins the thirty-eighth chapter.
Pauṣkara said:
The re-establishment of those infinite forms that existed on earth in various fields, having been lost over time, [is described]. (Pausa 38.1)
The gods and the perfected ones (siddhas) perform [their rites] by repeatedly calling to mind his form;
how could a dwelling be constructed by those who are unreal and subject to mortal conditions? (Pauṣa 38.2)
For the sake of uplifting his own lineage and also for the sake of his own fame,
the Blessed One said:
"Having worshipped with the mantra together with its ancillaries (sāṅga), accompanied by knowledge and meditation..."
O Pauṣkara, [this is achieved] through meditation, worship, and the practice of recitation.

And that which is the application of mantras to substances, elements, and forms—that indeed is the established consecration (pratiṣṭhā) for practitioners of mantra, characterized by its attainment. (Paus 38.4)
O twice-born one, at the end [of the rite], the mantra bestows the eternal perfection of mantras;
O Pauṣkara, this is because of the incapacity of those who know the mantras once they have died. (Pauṣkara 38.5)
And with a mind intent on favoring them, O Great-minded One, his sons and others, impelled by the Teacher, [should act] according to the prescribed rite and with that mantra. (Pauṣa 38.6)
Together with the mantras known as *ṛk* and *sāman*, which are joined with their respective pervasions,
one should practice with a mind that is attentive and engaged in worldly activity.
That which is performed as the middle [practice] is indeed the *pratiṣṭhā*; it bestows very little enjoyment, yet at the end of the body, it bestows a stainless and auspicious state. (Pauṣa 38.8)

Mental retention (dhāraṇā) is indeed accomplished through the Vedic mantras alone, characterized by their appropriate application at the proper time, together with meditation on the Lord and the ritual placement of mantras (nyāsa).
The Lord of Teachers should indeed perform [the rite] for his devotees toward the Supreme Lord;
it should be understood as common [to all], like a sacrifice that bestows the enjoyment of heaven. (Pauṣa 38.10)
O Lotus-born One, worshipped by the world, it should be understood that the fruit of mantra—whether pertaining to this life or the next—is dependent upon the teacher in this world. (Pausa 38.11)

Therefore, O Pauṣkara, he who possesses knowledge of reality, is learned in the scriptures, is devoted to right action, knows the six paths, and remains unconfused in every respect through his entire being— Pauṣkara 38.12.
Established by that, O Lotus-eyed One, the deity—whether moving or perfectly stable and vast—is firmly restrained therein by the mantra. (Pauṣa 38.13)
"Then, through the distinction between the moving and the stationary, it would become present.
Pauṣkara said:
"O Lord, by the mere passage of time, a substance undergoes the nature of decay."
For the essence of the mantra is imperceptible to people, yet it is worshipped by the world.
"What is awaited by those who know reality? Herein lies my great doubt.
The Blessed One replied:
"The Lord, assuming the form of a teacher, having set [the soul] free from the bondage of karma,"
For those who have taken refuge in various forms of devotion, as well as for those seeking various fruits [of their practice].
O high-minded one, having ascended that great and faultless power of fame belonging to those who perform actions, which fills the entire temple of the universe. (Pauṣa 38.16)
Pervaded by the rays of power through firm fortitude, she exists in the form of divine mantras and within the means consisting of mental states and ritual substances.
And she remains there for the sake of bestowing grace; thus it is celebrated as "Pratiṣṭhā.
Such is the arrangement consisting of material substances where the Lotus-Born One resides.

The rite known as *pratiṣṭhā* (consecration) is characterized by compassion and devotion; it constantly brings benefit to both [the practitioner and the deity], and indeed bestows the fruits of worldly prosperity (*śukti*) and liberation (*mukti*). (Pauṣkara 38.99)

And that [practice], O pure-eyed one, must always be performed as a duty by twice-born men established in the Brahman for the sake of self-realization; it is indeed forbidden [for others]. (Pauṣa 38.20)
And because of that fault, there is indeed no deliverance for them;
there is no end to it other than the fall of the body, yet that fall itself causes extreme suffering. (Pauṣa 38.21)
Therefore, from the very beginning, that must not be practiced by those of perfected self;
for it is always forbidden even to the four who have undertaken such actions.
One should always perform the proper installation of sacred objects with a mind intent on bestowing grace,
never out of a nature of obstruction, nor through greed, nor out of pride.
O Lotus-born One, when a sudden affliction such as a broken limb occurs, for the sake of compassion toward devotees, [one should act] with divine mantras, powers, and so forth. (Pauṣa 38.24)
When those [mantras] preceded by the twelve syllables— which are characterized by liberation as their sole fruit—
are fully worshipped, offered in sacrifice, and recited, they always effect atonement.

Therefore, O best of the twice-born, this [rite] should be performed with every effort by those possessing the three Vedas, by Kṣatriyas, by Vaiśyas, or even by Śūdras who are absorbed in the Blessed One.

Indeed, those with desires as well as those free from desires, intent on the propitiation of mantras, who have completed their Vedic studies, should always perform the installation of the image of the Blessed One. (Pauṣa 38.27)
Formerly, one who was to be propitiated, having first made a request,
was indeed established in a position of authority.
The best of the twice-born is a follower of the Pañcarātra.
He who is the knower of the manifest Supreme Self, preceded by its ritual array (*vyūha*), is always authorized to install the images of other Blessed Ones. (Pauṣkara 38.29)
Bestowing grace, establishing [the disciple], and defining the office—this is said to be the duty toward devoted followers who have attained [realization] through no other means. (Pauṣkara 38.30)
They were non-different [from him], knowers of the five times, who were not separate from him in the past;
born from his mouth before creation, they were contemplators of the twelvefold inner self.
Those for whom the arising and dissolution of things occurs through the supremacy of the fourfold manifestation,
they perform the renunciation of even their actions through the supervision of the Witness, in due order.
Therefore, another [person] who possesses supremacy toward that [goal] is even more difficult to find;
for him, there is a pure and manifest culmination of the objects of knowledge and a firm abiding in its practice.

Those situated on other paths do not accept the state of being "other" (paratva) with respect to one another; and for those who do accept it in relation to the Lord, there is no stability because of that very nature.
Indeed, he is one who has transcended all qualifications, who has attained the true aim, who is uncontrived,
devoted to the five times, pure, and has reached the further shore of the Tantric Siddhāntas.
Therefore, indeed, the injunction for all three types of Vedic mantras should be performed at each ritual action,
characterized by its appropriate occasion.

Because, in the case of activities such as the mandalas originating from the lotus, whether for one's own sake or for the sake of others, [this is done] during the constant rite of propitiation; (Paus 38.37)
O Pauṣkara, even though its form and its orientation toward that [reality] are eternally established, it will attain proximity for him in whose heart it has existence. (Pauṣkara 38.38)
The Lord of the World, the Supreme Self, the Imperishable Master, who is the very form of mantra— O Brahmin, even for the pleasure of the mind, he does not do so without great eagerness.
O twice-born one, that [consecration] was ordained by him for the sake of his desire or for the sake of his fame;
it is performed with the requisite means either in a temple or in one's own home. (Pauṣa 38.40)
Thus has the primary ritual procedure been correctly explained; hereafter, learn in brief that other secondary procedure which exists therein.

By twice-born ones who had previously received initiation according to rule, who were established in the dharma of the three Vedas, and who were devoted bhāgavatas of the Lord, constantly intent upon his worship; (38.42)

By those who have attained the objective of their ritual actions through the prior practice of retention and meditation, and who have exerted themselves in the application of mantras, mandalas, sacrificial pits, weapons, mudrās, and so forth; Paus 38.43.

By those who are established in the pervasion of the six paths, who are disposed toward renunciation, free from envy, who do not abandon the proper sequence, who are skillful, and who protect their own duties; Pausa 38.44.
When the consecration has been performed by those renowned for their good reputation in the world and those excluded from ill repute, the performer gains a firm standing. (Pauṣa 38.45)
O lotus-eyed one, this [rite] is always forbidden for others; likewise, the great festival known as Pratiṣṭhā is forbidden for those who perform mixed sacrifices. (Pauṣkara 38.46)
Pauṣkara said:
"O Lord, the practice of mixing [different rites] has been repeatedly forbidden;
yet you have consented to witness the sacrifices previously described."
"You ought to dispel now this doubt that has arisen regarding those very elements.
The Blessed One said:
"This is true, O one of great intelligence, just as it has been urged by you."
However, when another ritual action is encountered, there is no fault for those who possess the requisite qualification.
For all other beings possess an imperishable state of supreme devotion toward Acyuta, because the gods depend upon him; indeed, it is through the worship of others that this occurs. (Pauṣa 38.49)
For there is no fault in this, just as in the world there is none when brothers and groups of servants show honor to their lawful wives, whether in their presence or in their absence. (Pauṣya 38.50)
But those who abide in worldly dharmas, who have abandoned the state of equanimity,
and who do not know the distinction regarding the Blessed One, [act] always merely out of necessity.
For indeed, they all proclaim superiority by mere words—
those who, lacking the requisite qualification, are impelled here toward the worship of deities.
Thus, out of greed for remaining on the path, having understood their intention,
those who practice a mixture [of teachings] are established in a state of downfall.
Those who act in this very manner are surely led to hell;
but not so those whose souls are devoted to Vāsudeva and purified by true devotion.
O one of great intelligence, let it be that he might at times commit a fault or even cause injury; nevertheless, service should be performed with devotion. (Pauṣa 38.55)

For those devoted to the mantra through faith, if that mantra undergoes a transposition of syllables or is omitted by that [incorrect] vowel during the act of recitation, [the fault is remedied by devotion]. (Pauṣkara 38.56)
O Lotus-born One, although it is always superior by virtue of its vowels and other qualities, and bestows the single goal of the mantra upon its practitioners, nevertheless— Pausha 38.57.
And by the power of excessive devotion, he grants what is desired;
for to those who have taken refuge and are purified by true devotion, [he acts] without following a formal sequence.
The Lord of Mantras quickly bestows his grace upon those who have purified their selves;
how much more so, O Pauṣkara, for those who are perfected in ritual action and knowledge?
And for those who are devoted to faith and devotion, and have been instructed by teachers— therefore, O Mahāmati, for those who are perfectly serene in this teaching— (Paus 38.60)
All rites such as initiation and so forth for devotees are performed by those who are affectionate toward their devotees;
and even he who, not yet having attained me, performs [these rites] for the sake of attaining me.

For those beings who are devoted to the dull or mediocre [levels], whose minds delight in the enjoyment of sensual desires, my initiation (māmakī dīkṣā) or the installation [of images] and so forth may be performed even through delusion. (Pauṣa 38.62)
She leads away, before long, his own karma and the system of ritual action along with the seed of devotion to Him; even the supernatural powers turn their faces away.

O lotus-eyed one, having committed such great evil deeds, he shall quickly attain a miserable state even in this very life, and at the end of his body, having experienced this, he goes to a terrible hell.

Indeed, by the greatness of the Blessed One’s mantra and through the power of its activity, the evil arising from association perishes; yet, it may arise again due to the force of prior latent impressions.
Having further performed difficult penances, he may regain a human body;
he should then exert himself in pure conduct by which he may attain peace.
He certainly does not attain that teacher who is full of ego, devoid of devotion, and lacking authority; rather, he will surely obtain a hellish state according to his desire.
"O twice-born one, although the essence of mantra is omnipresent and bestows grace upon all, even so, it does not manifest its presence there. (Pauṣkara 38.68)
Even if one worships the image until the end of the body, one certainly does not enter into me;
at that very moment, spirits and vetālas cause the destruction of wealth and other possessions.
O Lotus-born One, those who are established in other philosophical systems are not to be favored;
likewise, a teacher should not be rejected by one who fears the terror of saṃsāra. (Pauṣa 38.70)
O Great Sage, for this very reason, one who is devoted solely to right devotion and is free from hypocrisy and passion [should perform] the supreme sacrifice known as Pratiṣṭhā.
"Indeed, that which is to be accomplished by Vaiṣṇavas must be done by Vaiṣṇavas from the very root.
Pauṣkara said:
"O Lord, for the four castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas who are devoted to the Blessed One..."
And for the sake of my welfare, I wish to know the very manner of Bimba’s birth.

The Blessed One said: For the sake of the gods, for the purpose of a journey to the forest, or for auspicious acts such as protection, when one has reached a region of the forest and performed that worship of the deities; Paus 38.73.
At the edge of the forest, with a perfectly pure mind and preceded by a sacrifice to the Blessed One, one should carry away a stone or a tree that is eternal.
Together with those who knew the Pañcarātra, as well as those devoted to the Ṛgveda and Sāmaveda,
he was accompanied by devotees intent on ritual action, pure and humble artisans.
Those who are self-restrained and initiated should first collect materials such as trees,
stones, minerals, or clay; then they should sprinkle the wombs of the earth with water.
